correctness.rationale: For |z|=W, t=W/2 and a=|z1|/2,b=|z2|/2, square overlap g_Q(z)=4(1-a)(1-b), a²+b²=t². Completing the square gives g/4=(1-t²)/2+(a+b-1)²/2, while s=a+b ranges over the full interval [t,√2t]. Projection of 1 onto that interval yields the exact minimum and complete directions; branch switch at W=√2. Bakaev–Polyanskii Corollary 7, Lemma 11 and Theorem 12 provide the needed planar general-plank-to-single-plank reduction; square erosion by ±z/2 is exactly g_Q(z). Direct uniform-convolution calculation for the centered plank verifies each optimum and strict center uniqueness. The small phase gap (W-√2)² and square-root angle onset follow by elementary trigonometry. Independent rational polygon clipping and dense angular checks confirm multiple W values, but the all-family conclusion rests on the inspected published reduction, not numerical single-plank optimization.
residual_risks: Only square side two, finite planks total W<2, Euclidean metric, one centered plank optimizer directions; no classification of all optimal multi-plank arrangements, general rectangles or W>=2.

final_claim: For Q=[-1,1]^2 and any 0<W<2, the maximal area covered by finite Euclidean planks of total width at most W equals 2√2 W-W²/2 up to W=√2 and 2+W²/2 afterwards. One centered plank attains the optimum. Its normals are diagonals at/below transition, otherwise |n1|+|n2|=2/W. Equivalently the square covariogram has the corresponding exact minimum at fixed Euclidean translation norm W, with an oblique direction bifurcation.
limitations: Only square side two, finite planks total W<2, Euclidean metric, one centered plank optimizer directions; no classification of all optimal multi-plank arrangements, general rectangles or W>=2.
